# Appeal of Denial – Spinal Fusion and Decompression (2026T0639I)

**Policy referenced:** Spinal Fusion and Decompression (2026T0639I)
Effective 2026-04-01
https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/spinal-fusion-decompression.pdf

**RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination**
Member: Jordan Iverson
Member ID: W979574719
Reference number: POC-E6EF62D505-92473
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-20
Requested service: Lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030)

Dear UnitedHealthcare / Oxford Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my lower back decompression surgery (CPT 63030), as stated in the notice dated 2026-08-20, reference number POC-E6EF62D505-92473. I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for my condition, and I believe the plan's own policy supports coverage.

## Why I believe this surgery meets the plan's own criteria

The plan's policy states: "Coverage Rationale Spinal procedures for the treatment of spine pain are proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances." My records show that I have had lower back pain for 9 months, and it has not gotten better with conservative treatment. Specifically:

- I completed 16 visits of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, over 10 weeks (2026-04-17 to 2026-06-26), as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I took NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-02, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- My MRI from 2026-06-17 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have radicular pain into my right calf.
- On exam, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit that matches the level shown on my MRI.

The plan's policy also states: "Surgery may be an option for individuals whose pain cannot be controlled by more conservative methods (National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases, 2023)." My records show exactly that — months of physical therapy, medication, and injection have not controlled my pain, and I now have a clear structural cause (nerve root compression from a disc extrusion) documented on imaging.

The policy further states: "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the: Procedures, Decompression +/- Fusion, Lumbar (Custom) - UHG Click here to view the InterQual® criteria." The denial notice does not tell me which specific InterQual criteria were applied to my case or why my documented findings did not satisfy them. Without that information, I am not able to see how the plan concluded that my records fall short.

The policy also notes: "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested." I understand that documentation alone does not guarantee approval, but I believe the records I have described directly address the standard the policy sets out — pain unrelieved by conservative care, supported by imaging findings and a corresponding neurologic exam.

## Request for the specific criteria applied

The plan's policy directs reviewers to InterQual® criteria for the medical necessity determination, but InterQual is licensed software and I do not have access to its full text. I am formally requesting, in writing, the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination, along with an explanation of which specific criterion or criteria my records did not meet. I understand I have a right to this information as part of the appeals process, free of charge.

## What I am asking for

I am asking the plan to reverse this denial and approve coverage for CPT 63030, or, at minimum, to provide the specific InterQual criteria applied to my case so that my surgeon and I can respond to any remaining questions directly. I have attached my physical therapy discharge note, medication and injection records, MRI report, and clinic notes documenting my exam findings in support of this appeal.

Please treat this letter as my formal appeal. I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-16, and I am submitting it through [member.uhc.com / the address printed on my denial letter — insert method used]. If you need additional records or have questions, you can reach me at the contact information below.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

________________________________
Jordan Iverson
Member ID: W979574719
Date: [insert date]
Phone: [insert phone number]
Email: [insert email address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

evidence.submission_route: Sign in at member.uhc.com and file the appeal there, or call the number on your card. There is no single public appeals fax or PO box — use the address on your denial letter. Online: member.uhc.com By phone: The number on your ID card Deadline: Usually 180 days from the denial -- but your denial letter is authoritative. Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter.
evidence.criteria_request: Your plan uses InterQual, which is licensed software rather than a public document. You have a right to it anyway: federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules require the plan to give you, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion relied on for the denial. Ask in writing for 'the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination'.
